themes_detail.label: Indoor Air Quality Crisis
themes_detail.summary: Indoor air quality complaints spiked to 12 this past week vs. a 3.9-complaint weekly average over the prior 8 weeks—a 210% increase (z-score: 4.43)—suggesting a potential widespread HVAC, mold, or ventilation failure affecting multiple buildings in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights this week.
evidence: 12 indoor air quality complaints filed last week vs. 3.9-week average over prior 8 weeks (210% spike)
Z-score of 4.43 indicates statistically significant anomaly (severity: high)
Timing clusters to single week, suggesting acute event rather than chronic issue
reporting_angles: Interview residents across affected buildings to identify common symptoms (respiratory, allergies, odors); determine if HVAC maintenance lapsed during winter transition
Contact NYC Department of Health & Mental Hygiene to determine if they've received related complaints; investigate whether landlords are responding to 311 filings

themes_detail.label: Construction Surge & Plumbing Failures
themes_detail.summary: General construction and plumbing complaints jumped to 31 last week vs. an 11.1-complaint weekly average—a 179% spike (z-score: 5.49)—indicating accelerated construction activity or widespread pipe/water system issues in the district this past week.
evidence: 31 construction/plumbing complaints last week vs. 11.1-week average over prior 8 weeks (179% increase)
Z-score of 5.49 indicates high statistical significance (severity: high)
1,013 total DOB building permits filed in last 90 days (753 alterations) suggests heavy renovation activity correlating with complaint spike
Timing aligns with potential winter thaw and pipe freeze-thaw damage common in early spring
reporting_angles: Cross-reference 311 complaint locations with active DOB permits to identify which projects are generating complaints; interview residents about noise, water shutoffs, or damage
Contact Department of Buildings to assess whether permit holders are adequately notifying tenants of work schedules and water disruptions

themes_detail.label: Derelict Vehicles Accumulation
themes_detail.summary: Derelict vehicle complaints surged to 12 two weeks ago vs. a 2.1-complaint weekly average—a 465% spike (z-score: 6.11)—indicating abandoned cars may be clustering in specific locations within Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights over the past 2 weeks.
evidence: 12 derelict vehicle complaints filed 2 weeks ago vs. 2.1-week average over prior 8 weeks (465% spike)
Z-score of 6.11 indicates severe statistical anomaly (severity: high)
Illegal Parking also ranks #1 concern overall with 6,190 complaints over 90 days, suggesting baseline enforcement challenges
reporting_angles: Map the 12 derelict vehicle complaints to specific blocks; visit those locations to photograph vehicles and document condition; determine how long they've been abandoned
Interview NYPD or NYC Department of Sanitation on enforcement timelines; ask why removals may be delayed and whether towing capacity is strained

themes_detail.label: Street Signs & Structural Hazards
themes_detail.summary: Dangling street sign complaints jumped to 6 last week vs. a 0.9-complaint weekly average—a 586% increase (z-score: 5.53)—alongside a separate 700% spike in hazardous materials complaints this past 3 weeks, suggesting potential windstorm damage or deferred maintenance affecting public infrastructure.
evidence: 6 dangling street sign complaints last week vs. 0.9-week average (586% spike, z-score: 5.53)
3 hazardous materials complaints 3 weeks ago vs. 0.4-week average (700% spike, z-score: 5.42)
Combined pattern suggests acute infrastructure failure event (weather-related or deferred maintenance breakdown) concentrated in 1-3 week window
reporting_angles: Review National Weather Service records for high winds or severe weather in Fort Greene/Brooklyn Heights 1-2 weeks prior; correlate timing with complaint filings
Contact NYC Department of Transportation to determine response time to dangling sign reports and identify streets with multiple reports; investigate whether maintenance backlog exists

themes_detail.label: Illegal Posting Epidemic
themes_detail.summary: Illegal posting complaints exploded to 4 three weeks ago vs. a 0.2-complaint weekly average—a 1500% spike (z-score: 8.66)—the highest z-score in the dataset, suggesting a targeted or widespread poster campaign (political, commercial, or nuisance-driven) hit the district 3 weeks ago.
evidence: 4 illegal posting complaints filed 3 weeks ago vs. 0.2-week baseline (1500% spike, z-score: 8.66—highest statistical anomaly in dataset)
Spike is now 2-3 weeks old; no indication of sustained elevation in most recent week, suggesting event-driven rather than ongoing crisis
reporting_angles: Visit neighborhoods to photograph and map remaining illegal postings; determine if they're political (election-related), commercial (real estate, nightlife), or nuisance-driven
Contact NYC Department of Sanitation to assess enforcement response and identify who filed complaints (community board, residents, BIDs)
